title: High-Rank Encoding Can Improve Approximate Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Conventional quantum-code constructions encode pure logical states as pure code states, but this restriction can sacrifice performance. We show that intrinsic encoding randomness can improve optimal entanglement fidelity. We bound the loss from imposing a rank-one encoder and prove it is at most quadratic near perfect recovery after joint optimization. The optimized advantage survives small noise perturbations. An explicit noise family requires higher-rank encoders arbitrarily close to perfect recovery, with every optimal encoder mapping pure inputs to mixed code states.
summary: This paper rigorously proves that for optimal approximate quantum error correction, restricting the encoder to rank-one mappings sacrifices performance compared to unrestricted encoding. The authors derive a precise, asymptotically quadratic lower bound for this performance gap, demonstrating that higher-rank encoders are necessary for achieving the true optimum.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether optimal approximate quantum error correction (AQEC) requires an encoder of rank higher than one, challenging the assumption that rank-one encoders suffice for optimal performance.
main_result: The authors prove that for entanglement fidelity, a higher-rank encoder is necessary to achieve the global optimum, establishing a strictly positive gap between the unrestricted and rank-one achievable fidelities.
method: The analysis uses entanglement fidelity as the objective function, deriving refined upper bounds on the infidelity gap by employing techniques like polar decomposition and analyzing the geometry of the error correction manifold.
model_or_system: The model is the general quantum error correction framework involving an encoder ($C$), a noise map ($N$), and a decoder ($D$). The analysis focuses on comparing the optimal fidelity achievable with unrestricted encoders versus those restricted to rank-one mappings.
key_observables: Entanglement fidelity ($F_e$), the optimized gap ($\Delta_{opt}$), and the asymptotic quadratic coefficient ($\kappa^{(2)}$) quantifying the difference between optimal and rank-one performance.
important_parameters: The small noise parameter ($\epsilon 	o 0+$) and the logical dimension ($d_L$) are crucial for determining the asymptotic behavior of the gap.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the encoder $C$ is a Completely Positive Trace Non-Increasing (CPTNI) map, and later relies on the existence of a global minimizer for the fidelity difference.
figures_summary: Figure 1(a) compares the derived upper bound on the infidelity gap against prior work. Figure 1(b) shows numerical estimates of the optimized gap versus infidelity for varying logical dimensions, comparing them to the derived asymptotic ceiling.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing general upper bounds on the gap using fidelity measures, to constructing specific noise families that demonstrate a positive gap, and finally employing advanced geometric analysis (tangent spaces, residual equivariance) to derive the exact asymptotic quadratic coefficient.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to quantify the performance limits of quantum error correction, which is fundamental to building fault-tolerant quantum computers. The explicit determination of the necessary encoder rank is a key theoretical result.
